Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

refer verb

pass on to someone or something else

also refer someone to, refer a matter to, be referred to

classical

Cic. Att. 9.13.8: ad ipsam tē epistulam rejiciō
Cic. Fam. 13.26.3: sī eōs … Rōmam rejēceris

rejiciō, rejicere, rejēcī, rejectum

verb, third conjugation; ad and the accusative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

refer (a person or a matter) to someone or something else

Lewis & Short: “to refer to, make over to, remand to”; of an official, to pass a matter on to another authority (rem ad senātum rejicere, often in Livy).

Other words

  • referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — refer (a question) to someone for a decision

    verb, irregular; ad and the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.122: ad Apollinem cēnseō referundum · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The consul’s word for laying a matter before the senate (ad senātum referre, Lewis & Short). Not “refer to” in the sense of mentioning (see mention) or meaning (see mean).

  • dēlēgō, dēlēgāre, dēlēgāvī, dēlēgātum — refer (someone to a book or a person); hand over (a task)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Nep. Cato 3.5 (Lewis & Short): studiōsōs Catōnis ad illud volūmen dēlēgāmus · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: “good prose; not in Caes.; perh. not in Cic.”.

Examples

  • sed nē bis eadem legās, ad ipsam tē epistulam rejiciō

    but so that you don’t read the same thing twice, I refer you to the letter itselfCic. Att. 9.13.8

  • dē rēbus et obscūrīs et incertīs ad Apollinem cēnseō referundum, ad quem etiam Athēniēnsēs pūblicē dē majōribus rēbus semper rettulērunt

    on things both obscure and uncertain I think one should refer to Apollo, to whom the Athenians too always referred their greater questions as a cityCic. Div. 1.122

See also mention, mean, forward.
